Czech EET 2.0 (Electronic Registration of Sales)

Registers contact payments received outside the till — cash, card or QR paid at the counter — with the Czech EET 2.0 system, keeps every data message with its confirmation code, retries until the tax authority has accepted it, and renews the cash-register certificate on its own.

Version19.0.1.3.0
EditionCommunity and Enterprise
LicenceAGPL-3
Requiresbase, account, mail
Extended byl10n_cz_eet2_pos

What it is for

From 1 January 2027 every Czech business that takes contact payments — money received in personal contact with the customer or in its premises, whether cash, a card on the terminal or a QR code scanned at the counter — must report each such sale to the Financial Administration (Finanční správa) at the moment it happens. This is EET 2.0, the second edition of the electronic registration of sales.

This module is the Odoo side of it. It holds the cash-register certificate (pokladní certifikát) issued by the Financial Administration, builds and signs the data message for each sale, sends it to the EET 2.0 gateway and stores the confirmation code (POK, potvrzovací kód) that comes back. Sales made at a Point of Sale till are registered by l10n_cz_eet2_pos; this module registers the contact payments booked in accounting — a customer paying an invoice in cash at the office, a card payment taken at the counter, a QR code scanned in the shop.

Legal background

The act on the registration of sales (zákon o evidenci tržeb), No. 180/2026 Sb., in force from 1 January 2027. Certificates and evidence units can be set up in the tax portal from 1 November 2026, and the production gateway accepts messages from that date in a transitional regime.

  • A registered sale is a payment received in personal contact with the business, or in its premises or vehicle in connection with the goods or service (§ 5 and § 6). The payment method is irrelevant: cash, card, bank transfer, QR code, vouchers, tokens or crypto-assets all count when they happen that way. The same QR code paid from home is not a contact payment.
  • The sale must be registered no later than when it takes place. For a card or QR payment that moment is when the customer issues the payment order, not when the money arrives (§ 16 odst. 2).
  • The message carries only the taxpayer's EIČ, the evidence unit, the cash register, a sequence number, the date and time, and the total amount in CZK (§ 17). No items, no VAT breakdown, no customer data, no payment method.
  • The business sets a response time limit of at least 2 seconds (§ 19). When the gateway does not answer in time, the sale still goes through and the message must be sent as soon as the cause has passed, at the latest within 48 hours; the duty does not lapse after that (§ 20).
  • A refund or correction is registered as a negative sale (§ 8).
  • Top-ups and redemptions of gift cards, e-wallets and similar means usable only in a limited network are registered in two dedicated items (§ 17 odst. 2); see l10n_cz_eet2_pos_loyalty.
  • The act requires no receipt. Printing the POK on a receipt is voluntary.
  • The EIČ is the taxpayer's DIČ (§ 18). Certificates are valid for one year.

Whether a given payment is a contact payment is a judgement for you and your adviser; the module records what you flag, it does not decide for you.

Setting it up

1. In the tax portal

In MOJE daně → DIS+, register your evidence units (evidenční jednotky: each shop, vehicle or "outside premises" activity). Each receives a number, two to nine digits ending in 1 to 4. Then generate one or more cash-register certificates and download each as a .p12 file with its password.

2. Company settings

Accounting → Configuration → Settings, block Czech EET 2.0, tick Enable EET 2.0:

Setting What it does
EET 2.0 Environment Playground for testing, Production for real sales. A playground confirmation code ends in -ff and fulfils no legal duty.
EET 2.0 Taxpayer EIC Your EIČ, CZ plus 8 to 10 digits. Pre-filled from the company's VAT number when that has the right shape.
EET 2.0 Default Unit ID The evidence unit number from DIS+ used when a journal or till names none.
EET 2.0 Certificate The certificate messages are signed with; see below.
EET 2.0 Response Time Limit (s) How long a till waits for the gateway before letting the sale through, at least 2 seconds, 5 by default.
EET 2.0 Warn After Attempts After this many failed attempts a warning is logged. Sending itself never stops.
EET 2.0 Renew Certificate (days before expiry) How many days before a certificate expires its renewal starts automatically; 0 switches renewal off.

3. Certificates

EET 2.0 → Configuration → Certificates: create a record per certificate, pick its environment, upload the .p12 and enter its password. The EIČ in the certificate and its validity are read from the file. Test certificate sends a message in verification mode: the gateway checks everything and answers without recording a sale, so you can prove the certificate and the connection on the production gateway without registering anything. A playground certificate can only be used against the playground, and the other way round.

4. Which payments are registered

On each bank or cash journal, tab Advanced Settings, block Czech EET 2.0:

Field What it does
EET 2.0 Contact Payments New customer payments in this journal are proposed as contact payments.
EET 2.0 PoS ID (id_pokl) The cash register name sent for this journal, up to 20 characters; the journal code when empty.
EET 2.0 Unit ID (id_jednotky) The evidence unit for this journal; the company default when empty.

Every customer payment then carries its own EET 2.0 Contact Payment flag, proposed from the journal and editable until the sale is accepted. This is where you tell the two cases apart that the law treats differently and that land on the same bank account: a QR code scanned at the counter (tick) and the same code paid from home (untick). Payments received from suppliers are never registered, and neither are the payments Odoo books when a Point of Sale session closes — the till has already registered those orders.

How a sale is registered

When a flagged payment is posted, Odoo queues a message and the scheduled job sends it within about two minutes. EET 2.0 → Messages lists them all, and each payment shows its EET 2.0 Status, its EET 2.0 POK and an EET 2.0 button opening its messages.

Status Meaning
To Send, Retry Scheduled Waiting for the next attempt.
Accepted The gateway issued a POK. Done.
Verified A verification-mode test succeeded; no sale was recorded.
Rejected The gateway refused the message for good (invalid signature, wrong EIČ, schema error). Fix the cause and press Requeue.
Error The message could not be built, typically because no valid certificate was available. It is retried hourly and re-queued automatically when a certificate is uploaded or selected.

What happens when the gateway is unreachable follows the act: attempts are repeated with growing intervals until 48 hours after the sale, then every hour for as long as it takes. A message that crosses the 48-hour line is flagged Past 48 h and an activity is raised for an EET 2.0 manager, so the backlog never ages in silence. Every attempt is a new message with a new identifier, as the Financial Administration's methodology requires; the earlier identifiers stay on the record under Previous attempts, and the request and response XML are kept for support.

Refunds and reversals. Resetting a posted payment to draft or cancelling it registers a negative sale of the same amount, dated at the reversal, in the same cash register and sequence. Posting the payment again registers a new sale. A customer refund paid out from a flagged journal is registered as a negative sale as well.

Amounts. The message is always in CZK. A payment in another currency is converted at the company's rate for the day of the sale, and the original amount and currency are kept on the message.

Certificate renewal

A cash-register certificate lives one year. The module renews it through the Financial Administration's CA EET 2.0 service without a visit to the portal: the set number of days before expiry it asks for a follow-up certificate, downloads it as a new certificate record, sends a verification-mode message with it, and only when the gateway accepts does it switch the company to the new certificate, archive the old one and confirm the download to the authority. Renew with CA EET on the certificate runs the same cycle by hand, and the Renewal status shows where it stands. When the verification fails or the authority rejects the request, the old certificate stays in use and an EET 2.0 manager gets an activity. A separate daily check raises warnings 30, 14 and 7 days before expiry.

Limitations

  • The address of the certificate authority for playground certificates is our reading of the published specification, which lists three environments without saying which non-production one serves the playground. Production renewal is unaffected. Both addresses are system parameters an administrator can change.
  • The module cannot tell a contact payment from a remote one; the journal default and the payment flag are your decision.
  • A copy of a production database must not register sales. Odoo's database neutralisation (used by Odoo.sh staging builds and duplicate with neutralise) switches EET 2.0 off on every company of the copy; certificates and settings stay, so the copy can be switched back on against the playground.
  • The EET OFF regime for the smallest sole traders is a choice made with the tax office, not a setting here; a company in it simply leaves EET 2.0 off.
  • Registration on behalf of another taxpayer (pověření, zastoupení) is carried in the message but has no configuration screen yet.
